scene clearnightsky
Would it be too poetic of me to say that my heart is still in McDonald’s?
Probably. Yes. But that’s how it feels.

And somewhere along the lines, I parted ways with Yasu, failed to get into contact with Ayane, and let the ghost of me clean off my table at a cheap fast-food restaurant while my body went off on its own.
I’m back at the hotel now — or at least my aforementioned body is. And it rests on a cold, half-circular seat in the lobby approximately ten feet away from the door.
Every time it opens, it feels like the weather is trying to warn me that I’d be better off outside its half-circle of influence.
Beneath the covers — my head in the sand of a beach I now long for disguised as a sheet. But as the ghost handles the hard labor, I get to labor over what I think is hard.
And right now, that’s preventing myself from returning to the six-armed triumvirate of monks that guided me through the last iteration of half of this holiday.
Basically, I feel dead. Overwhelmed. But without knowing why, all I can really do is sit idly by and either wait for it to blow over or wait for someone else to distract me.
And surely you know which option I chose.
scene nodokaboilertime1
I find myself curious about the weather up north — and how much colder it must be than Hell.
The answer is ten degrees Celsius when we assume that Hell is here. Which it isn’t because Shakespeare said that Hell is empty and I guess the devils came to Kumon-mi instead.
But as they bash my skull with their twangling instruments, pick the coral from my bones and pearls from my eyes, I have just enough time to acknowledge a thing of darkness that is mine.
Hark! Now, I hear them. Those endless violent knocks. “When’s the last time that I slept?” I think. Is it me these birds must mock?
My light’s burnt out, I can not glow. And you left me out to rot.
So all that’s left for me to do is sit around and think about what Gossamer forgot.
scene nodokaboilertime2
: Hah...
Shakespeare also said that misery acquaints a man with strange bedfellows. And oh, how many unicorns have wound up in mine.
Awake, dear heart, awake. You lazy piece of shit. You have a job to do.
Just smoke your fucking cigarette and let the endorphins wash over you like the waves of the Mediterranean swelling at Prospero’s hand.
: Good evening, Akira.
scene nodokaboilertime3
: Your message seemed rather urgent. I came as quickly as I could.
There she is — my cancer. The coming storm that will drown me in my very own book.
: Something’s wrong and I don’t know what it is. And if I spend one more second waxing poetic, I’m pretty sure you’ll be able to make candles out of my cerebral cortex.
: Oh? Then perhaps it’s best to let you stew in the freedom of thought for just a tad bit longer. A candle would be such a simple way to keep a piece of you near me at all times.
: I need you to take my mind off of things again. You’re still willing to do that for me, right?
scene nodokaboilertime4
: A booty call at this hour? With so many other suitors still lining the halls like Christmalloween lights? Akira, you spoil me.
: I just...I need something. This isn’t like the other times I’ve felt off, Nodoka. It’s like something’s just gone and I can’t put my finger on what.
: And you would bestow the honor of absorbing such feelings unto me? After I was such a bad girl last time?
: You mean when you fucked me into unconsciousness at the beach? Yeah, whatever. Do that again. I welcome it this time. Experiment away.
scene nodokaboilertime5
: Are you sure a lap pillow wouldn’t suffice? With the way you are now, I can’t help but worry that you’ll soil my dress.
: I’ll buy you a new one. Just come with me to a love hotel and-
scene nodokaboilertime6
: A love hotel? Do you take me for some sort of harlot? Have you no room of your own this time?
: I don’t think so. I haven’t had much time to really mingle this year between my apocalyptic brainstorming and buying ice cream for a religious fanatic.
: What an exciting day you’ve had. And here I was thinking that mine would be hard to beat.
: Are we doing this or not? Because I can text someone else.
: If you do, can I watch? I’m quite nervous about the damage you will do to me in your current state. I’m still just a fragile little nymph, you see. And you’re a very big boy, Akira.
: Okay, fine. Go back upstairs then. I’ll find someone else.
scene nodokaboilertime7
: Okay, okay. I apologize. I see you’re in no mood for jokes tonight.
: I’m more than willing to...hear you out again. But I’d like to remind you that there is more than one way to quiet the isle once it’s full of noises, Akira.
: Like what? You want to talk? About birds again? Let’s just cut to the part that works.
: May I at least ask you a question first?
: Why? Is it about hugging again?
: I’m just curious as to whether or not you’re being rude to me because you don’t think of me as a girl or if your mood is really just that bad.
: Because it may not seem like it at times, but I have feelings too. And quite the contrary to a certain individual, mine are rather colorful tonight.
: Well, I’m very happy for you. Mine aren’t.
: Yes, you’ve made that quite clear. But will you not even hear me out?
: Because I have no intention of letting you use me if I get nothing in return, Akira. You don’t have nearly enough Nodoka points for that yet.
: Can you tell me while I am using you like a fleshlight?
: It may be difficult, but I’m willing to try.
: Deal. Let me see if there’s a vacant room here or-
scene nodokaboilertime8
: There’s no need.
: I know somewhere we won’t be disturbed...
scene black
scene nodokaboilertime9
: The boiler room. How very Nodoka.
: How beauteous the darkness is! O brave new hideaway, that has such people in it!
scene nodokaboilertime10
: Oh, good. Can you read minds too now? Because if I have to deal with two of you back-to-back, I’m not sure if I’ll even be able to get it up.
: Not at all. It just wasn’t hard to decipher that a man such as yourself would find comfort in the Tempest as his emotions swelled like the waves of a storm born from Prospero’s hand.
scene nodokaboilertime11
: And also — your first love was quite the bardolater, wasn’t she? Is that where your affinity for Shakespeare comes from?
: Well?
scene nodokaboilertime12
: Let us not burden our remembrance with a heaviness that's gone.
: Ah! But I long to hear the story of your life, which must captivate the ear strangely.
: You know enough already, Nodoka.
: I do. But your tale, sir, would cure deafness. And as it stands, will I ever truly get it if all I have are the Cliffnotes?
: Just fill in the blanks yourself. You’re a writer. Hell, you’ll probably make my story even more interesting that way.
: Ahh, but that’s where you’re mistaken. For there are times when even reality trumps fiction, Akira. That’s becoming all the more apparent to me with each passing moment.
: Cool. Can we have sex now?
: You taught me language, and my profit on't...
scene nodokaboilertime13
: Is, I know how to curse...
: You know how to kill the mood as well.
: I’m a pacifist, Akira. I do not kill anything. I am merely setting the stage for what is sure to be the dicking of a lifetime. Apologies if I want that to be special.
: Why are you so interested in me anyway? Like...yes. I’m the Boy. But now that you know, what’s the point? Why dig deeper? She’s dead. There’s nothing more to learn.
: But did you see her die?
scene nodokaboilertime14
: I did actually. Want me to recount it right now? Will hearing about her skull fragments decorating the concrete get you wet?
: It might if you describe it like that. Is it getting hot in here, or is it maybe just all of the boilers?
: Sorry, are you trying to piss me off? Is this how you...what, get me to black out again? Is that the goal here?
scene nodokaboilertime15

: I have no desire to hurt you, Akira. You’re the closest thing to both a father and a lover that I’ve ever had. And surely you know how precious such a combination must be to a pervert like me, don’t you?
: Yes. So why won’t you just take the pain away already? I don’t want to talk right now. I want this to be over.
: Ahh — and there’s the rub.
scene nodokaboilertime16
: For there can be no end to this vicious cycle. And I mean that in more ways than one, if you catch my drift.
: I don’t care about your fucking-
: Think, Akira. Calm your mind and think of what I just said.
: I...I don’t...
scene nodokaboilertime17
: You do, though. You just don’t want to believe it.
: Nodoka-
scene nodokaboilertime18
: I had a dream last night — that a great disaster consumed this world. And as it went, so did we. But to where was not exactly clear.
: For it was a place that looked just like this one. Just as depraved and sad and lost among the stars, entirely unremarkable once removed from the lens of a microscope.
: In that dream, everything stopped but me. And I roamed the lands in search of answers to all of the questions I struggle to ask when that thing we call “life” flourishes around us.
: It was quite boring for a dream, really. There was no monster threateningly following behind me, silently waiting for the right time to pounce.
: But there was a girl. One who seems more like a silhouette in hindsight — who smelled of coriander and tobacco — looming in the background, existing somewhere she shouldn’t.
: Have you ever had a dream like that, Akira?

scene nodokaboilertime19
: A dream where something that shouldn’t exist does? Whether it be from another world...or another time perhaps?
: It’s happening again...
: What is?
: That...feeling. That there’s something that’s supposed to be there and it’s just not anymore.
: Ayane must have felt it too. That’s why she-
scene nodokaboilertime20
: Ngh!?
: This is how they want you to feel, Akira! The doors I chase after are not the kind that we are meant to open!
: People like us are destined to queue outside and wait for the chance to get in! It’s no wonder that everything I’ve done has amounted to nothing so far!
: The trick was to stop looking! Let the answers come to us instead!
scene nodokaboilertime21
: And come they did — for in this moment, where everything seems so blurry to you, my sight has never been so clear.
: (DIALOGUE FORCIBLY CENSORED. THIS CHARACTER HAS BEEN CORRUPTED.)
: If it’s god that you fear, why not become one yourself?
scene nodokaboilertime22
: Or, if that won’t work, hide.
: For they can find us here in Kumon-mi, or even in our heads.
: But there is somewhere out there beyond the reach of god that I know we can get to if we can find the right door and someone to open it.
: Maybe that’s where you’ll find what you’re looking for.
scene nodokaboilertime23
: But in the meantime, you have me.
: And despite how mad I may make you...or how desperately you flail as you attempt to decipher the often meaningless things I have to say...
: Despite all that, you will never be alone. For there will always be someone twice as capable, searching three times as hard for something four times bigger.
: And I like you enough to share what I find.
: Yet I can’t help but wonder if you’d do the same for me?
: Nodoka...just for clarity’s sake...
: Do you know that we’re caught in a timeloop?...
: I had a feeling.
: I just wanted to hear it from a different horse’s mouth this time.
scene nodokaboilertime24
: Now — I believe this is the part where you take me.
